Not for redistribution without written consent of Morgan Stanley Morgan Stanley RESEARCH Idea February 9, 2026 05:01 AM GMT US Technology | North America Global Cloud Capex Tracker: Another Year Of 60%+ Growth Cloud capex continues to surprise to the upside, with 2026 aggregate spending now $735B, the 3rd consecutive year of 60% + growth. As demand for compute continues to outstrip supply, we expect strong cloud capex announcements to persist, a positive for suppliers with elevated exposure to cloud capex. Key Takeaways Consensus Global Cloud capex is now $735B in 2026, 22 pts higher than a week ago, and equivalent to ~60% Y/Y growth. Capital spending intensity amongst the 11 top global spenders is now >25% of total revenue, 3x the 2014-2023 average. Total global cloud capex in 2025-2026 is now $1.2T, $500B higher than was forecasted a year ago. We see this as a clear positive for component suppliers with elevated exposure to cloud capex. 2026 cloud capex is now tracking to ~$735B, or ~60% Y/Y growth, 22 points, or ~$120B, higher than pre-4Q earnings ( Exhibit 2 ). The uptick in 2026 capex is driven by the strong CY26 capex guidance issued by GOOGL, AMZN, and META this earnings season ( Exhibit 3 ). And while 57% Y/Y growth in 2026 would imply a 9- point Y/Y deceleration vs. 2025, it would also mark the third consecutive year that the 11 top cloud capex spenders, collectively, grow capital expenditures ~60%+ Y/Y, unprecedented in the history of our cloud capex tracker. It wouldn't surprise us if Consensus cloud capex estimates move higher from here as well given (1) MSe aggregate capex is $795B, 8% above Consensus, and (2) aggregate cloud capex estimates for the top 11 spenders has increased every quarter for, at least, the last 9 quarters. In fact, if we go back to a year ago (pre-4Q24 earnings), 2025-2026 aggregate Global Cloud capex was forecasted at $710B. Today, it's forecasted at $1.2T, or an incremental $500B of spending, equivalent to 26% of aggregate revenue, ~3x the 2014-2023 capital spending intensity average ( Exhibit 4 ). As monthly tokens processed grows exponentially ( Exhibit 5 ), aggregate cloud revenue for GCP/AWS/Azure accelerates ( Exhibit 7 ), data center commitments expand, and data center component suppliers highlight accelerating demand and elongating visibility, we believe there will continue to be upward pressure on hyperscaler capex estimates. What specifically are the big 4 US hyperscalers saying about 2026 spending plans? US hyperscaler commentary this earnings season continues to underscore an extraordinary acceleration in AI driven infrastructure spending heading into 2026, with all of them signaling both persistent supply constraints throughout 2026 and the need for accelerated investment and/or optimizing capacity allocation to address surging compute demand. META guided to 2026 capex of $115-135B (+73% Y/Y at midpoint), with heavier investment in Meta Superintelligence Labs (MSL) and broader AI infrastructure needs. GOOGL guided to 2026 capex of $175-185B (+97% Y/Y at midpoint), with spending ramping throughout the year to support Google DeepMind, user facing AI improvements across Google Services, and significant cloud infrastructure demand. GOOGL noted that ~60% of spend is on servers and 40% on long duration assets such as data centers and networking. AMZN expects to spend ~$200B in capex in 2026 (+52% Y/Y), predominantly for AWS, driven by both faster-than-anticipated growth in core (non AI) and AI cloud workloads. AMZN also noted that it is monetizing capacity as fast as it can install it. MSFT didn't provide a quantitative guidance for 2026, but signaled that its March quarter capex will decline Q/Q due to normal variability from cloud ingrastructure build outs and the timing of delivery of finance leases. MSFT management also noted that the capex mix of short-lived assets (CPU and GPU servers) will remain ⅔, similar to the December quarter.
